title: Chromolitho calendar plate

reference.grammar: chromolithograph scan: flat tint plates ~1 px out of register against a soft dark olive-brown keyline; tiled ornament border cut by an arc; botanical panels; typeset calendar

units: design units, 1000 = plate width (ref 622 px ⇒ 1 u = 0.622 ref px; 1 ref px = 1.61 u); plate is 1000 × 1447 u

ground.tooth: ±1.1 % per-pixel noise before the softness pass (ref paper L std 1.6)

techniques.name: Olive-brown keyline

params.register_offset: none; the keyline is the reference plate

techniques.implementation: Every silhouette and rule is a polyline displaced by 3-octave sine noise of arc length (amp 0.7 u) and stroked in 8-point runs whose width varies ±15 %, into one keyline canvas multiplied over the sheet last.

techniques.name: Plate register offset + knockout

params.knockout: every fill erases its shape (destination-out) from all other plates and the keyline canvas, so plates do not overprint; the offsets then leave paper slivers and overlaps at every edge

techniques.implementation: Each tint plate is an offscreen canvas whose base transform is translated by its offset; a fill knocks its polygon out of the other plates, then all plates are multiplied onto a white sheet, mottled, and multiplied onto the paper.

techniques.name: Flat tint plate
techniques.implementation: Polygons filled with the plate ink at full opacity, with no gradients or tone; the keyline does all the modeling.

techniques.name: Print mottle on inks
techniques.implementation: ImageData pass over the composited sheet: every non-white pixel is multiplied by 1 ± 0.022·hash(⌊x/cell⌋,⌊y/cell⌋); white (paper) pixels are untouched.

techniques.name: Scan softness

params.passes: round(0.6 u · S · dpr / 0.7), min 1 (1 at 700 css px @ dpr 2)
params.measured_on_ref: keyline runs 1–2 px dark but 2.7 px integrated darkness

techniques.implementation: After compositing, one ImageData pass applies a horizontal then vertical 3-tap binomial blur so keylines and dot screens carry the reference scan’s soft edges instead of crisp anti-aliasing.

techniques.name: Scallop (fish-scale) tile
techniques.implementation: Staggered rows of keyline semicircles (r = pitch/2) over a light-ochre field, a keyline dot at each arc center, clipped to the band; rust rule beneath.

techniques.name: Spiral tile
techniques.implementation: On a hex-staggered 52 u grid each spiral is an Archimedean polyline (r = 3.5 → r_max over 1.3–1.5 turns) offset along its normals into a ribbon, knocked out of the pale plate, filled slate and keylined; a black dot sits in each gap.

techniques.name: Square-and-dot tile
techniques.implementation: Ochre field with paper squares cut out (destination-out on the plate), each square keylined with a wavered outline, keyline dots on the half-pitch lattice.

techniques.name: Heart tile
techniques.implementation: Light-ochre field with paper hearts (two arcs and a point) cut out and keylined; a row of black squares alternates between heart rows.

techniques.name: Running-scroll band
techniques.implementation: Slate ribbon spirals every 60 u joined by a quadratic wave ribbon, each knocked out of the pale ground and keylined, black dot in the trough.

techniques.name: Wave band

params.vertical_variant: 7 lines at 21.7 u pitch, wavelength 30 u, amp 4 u, 4 u ribbon, in the right column 626–1160 u

techniques.implementation: Sine polylines stroked as slate ribbons on pale gray, each with a thin keyline along one edge.

techniques.name: Salmon dot screen
techniques.implementation: Salmon field, then a darker salmon plate of jittered discs on a 9.5 u hex lattice knocked out of the ground, both under the keyline.

techniques.name: Rust zigzag rule
techniques.implementation: A rust polyline zigzag between two rust rules, on the rust plate, over paper.

techniques.name: Checker band
techniques.implementation: Alternate 12 u cells filled on the black plate; keyline rules top and bottom.

techniques.name: Star-sprig lunette

params.sprig: 6 keyline rays 3.5→8–10.5 u round a dot

techniques.implementation: Peach plate clipped to the arch, keyline star sprigs on a staggered lattice with a dot between.

techniques.name: Great arc

rings.tile: ring-and-dot on pale gray, pitch 20 u, ring r 6.2

techniques.implementation: Concentric clip discs drawn over the right column and the calendar bands (each ground knocked out of what lies beneath): inner ochre square tile, ring-and-dot band, a salmon band, a sawtooth ring of black triangles, each ring keylined.

techniques.name: Keyline botanical

asters.disc: 0.30 R ochre, 34 keyline stipple dots r 1.2

params.leaves: lanceolate, width sin(πt)^0.8, length 85–160 u, width 13–20 u, keyline midrib 1.6 u

techniques.implementation: Each organ is a closed polyline built from cubics/quads, knocked out of the plates beneath, filled on its plate and keylined; asters are 15–17 two-quad petals round an ochre disc; goldenrod plumes are arcs of ochre dots with keyline crescents.

techniques.name: Hop frieze

params.leaves: 3-lobed serrate hop leaf, #AD834C, size 44–70 u, keyline veins
params.bines: sage ribbon 4.5–5 u keylined, tendril spiral r 10
params.band: dot screen 1222–1302 u, wave band 1306–1342 u

techniques.implementation: Hop cones rise above the salmon band as ovoid pale-yellow silhouettes carrying six rows of downward keyline bract scallops; tan lobed leaves and sage bines cross the dot screen.

techniques.name: Zodiac cartouche (Virgo)

params.ground: #C5BB7F strip with 1.3 u keyline grass hatch every 6 u
params.rays: 30 keyline rays 1.1 u α0.55 from r 70–90 to 150–190 round (180,236)

sheaf.body: pale-yellow hourglass 104 u wide at base, 24 u at the waist, 168 u at the ears
sheaf.grain: ochre ovals 9×3.6 u in pairs, awns 20 u

params.tab: cream box 140×46 u at y 14, ochre bosses r 9, ♍ from three arches + looped tail in 3 u keyline

techniques.implementation: Double-ruled square; sky plate, horizon strip, rays from a point behind the sheaf; the sheaf body is one knocked-out polygon with keyline stalks fanning through it, bound by a tan band, each stalk ending in an ear of alternating ochre grains with thin awns.

techniques.name: Typeset calendar

weekdays.letters: S M T W T F S

techniques.implementation: canvas fillText/strokeText on the green, dark-green, red and keyline plates (each with its own register offset); the month is a light green fill with a dark green outline like the reference’s decorated serif.

techniques.name: Cream paper

params.noise: ±1.1 % per pixel, hashed, before the softness pass

techniques.implementation: Flat fill plus a hashed per-pixel brightness noise; nothing else is drawn on the paper except ink.

pass_order: tile fields (clipped to rules) on their plates
arc rings over the column and bands
botanicals: left panel, top-right cluster, bottom-left bine, frieze
composite plates with offsets in multiply onto white
notes: Colors are per-region k-means centers on ref-04.png (paper is the modal pixel 241,229,203); keyline width from 266 line crossings (2.7 px integrated darkness incl. scan blur ⇒ ≈1.4–1.7 px ink).
Reference shares at 96 px: paper 0.44, black ≈0.024, light ochres ≈0.10; mean L 190.
Seed 4404; layout 1000 × 1447 u: left column 60–300, calendar 310–790, right column 800–952, frieze 1170–1342, frame 48–962 × 30–1372.
